name: Kon Tum coffee
summary: Vietnam Tourism calls Kon Tum the coffee hub of the Central Highlands and describes the highland bean as Robusta. Go Vietnam’s cluster article calls the local cup arabica. Both claims stay. A single cup price does not.
origin: Vietnam Tourism calls Kon Tum the Kingdom of Coffee. Dak Ha, just north of downtown, holds over 9,000 hectares, which that article also prints as over 22,000 acres.
howToEat: Vietnam Tourism describes cà phê sữa đá as a slow drip through a phin, with condensed milk and ice, and cites Bloomberg Businessweek in 2019 for that cup. The café is the social hub: people do not drink it alone. The same article says cafés also pour juices and sometimes serve meals. A cup price was not printed there.

Go Vietnam’s cluster article calls it Kon Tum arabica, brewed in a phin, at 25,000–40,000 VND a cup, and roasted ground beans at 200,000–400,000 VND a kilogram. Go Vietnam’s Măng Đen article says the 1,200-metre plateau suits arabica, a light cup with a mild sour finish, at 30,000–60,000 VND. The bean and the price disagree across these publishers. Check on arrival.
Drink it in the morning or after the river walk. Vietnam Tourism describes cafés looking over the Đăk Bla. A street clock was not printed. Check on arrival.
where: City cafés, and the Dak Ha coffee belt north of town on Vietnam Tourism. Măng Đen is the other cup, on Go Vietnam, at 1,200 metres.
seoTitle: Kon Tum coffee — Robusta or arabica
seoDescription: Vietnam Tourism calls the highland bean Robusta and Dak Ha a 9,000-hectare belt. Go Vietnam prints arabica at 25,000–40,000 VND in town and 30,000–60,000 VND in Măng Đen.
